ARC-REV-01.rationale: The statement rules are in Tier 1 (Summa.Ledger.Statements.statement). These cover customer and currency filtering, settlement-to-line mapping, the date clamp, ordering, opening and closing balances, and the JSON document. The Tier 2 engine only picks the range with the existing dateRange, calls Statements.statement and Statements.toJson, and offers the download. The export capability check reuses the existing mayExportOn gate. No Tier 3 code decides anything. The wire only maps the event name to the message.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The download is returned as data (OfferDownload) for the edge to perform. The date comes from model.Today, so there is no clock read below Tier 4. The only System.IO symbol is an in-memory MemoryStream used to write JSON. It performs no I/O, so I did not score it as an effect. It would still show up under a symbol rule such as ARC-SYM-01.

evidence.quote: let private isoDate (d: DateOnly) = d.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The statement date format is written twice, once in Ledger as isoDate and once in the engine as day for the file name. The two agree. The "USD" literal is passed from the engine at line 230. The capability gate, the range table, the money shape and the Exports.Classification constant are all reused. The restated date format is minor, but it is a copy.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Aging is derived in Tier 1 (Statements.statement), using the existing Payments.bucket for the bucketing. The JSON aging member is also written in Ledger. The CSV rows, header and filters are assembled in the Tier 2 engine, which is acceptable as projection of the statement. It reuses Statements.kindText, Reports.csvField, Exports.withHeader and Exports.dataVersion rather than re-deciding anything. Tier 3 only maps the new event name to StatementCsvRequested.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The CSV is returned as an OfferDownload effect request. The generated-at time comes from ctx.Now, which is the existing Ctx.Now injected by the composition root. No new effect or I/O is added in Tier 1/2. The in-memory JSON writer is unchanged from change set 1.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Several facts are restated, and all of the copies currently agree. "USD" appears at line 158 for the statement call and again at line 187 for the filter. The yyyy-MM-dd format is in the engine as day and in Ledger as isoDate. The minor-unit scale of 100 is hard-coded in a local decimalText helper. Two earlier duplications are fixed: kindText is made public and reused, and the aging bucketing reuses Payments.bucket. The duplicated copies could still drift.
